what_its_for: Levoleucovorin is used for two main purposes: (1) It acts as a 'rescue' medication to protect healthy cells from the harmful effects of a cancer drug called methotrexate. (2) It is also used together with a chemotherapy drug called fluorouracil (5-FU) to help treat advanced colorectal (colon and rectal) cancer. Think of it as a vitamin-like helper that either shields your body from methotrexate toxicity or makes certain chemotherapy work better.
how_to_take: Levoleucovorin is given by a healthcare provider as an injection into your vein (intravenous or IV) or into a muscle. You will NOT give this medication to yourself at home. It is always administered in a clinic, hospital, or infusion center by a trained nurse or doctor. Each treatment session may take anywhere from a few minutes to several hours depending on your treatment plan.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your exact dose based on your body size, the condition being treated, your kidney function, and the specific chemotherapy drugs you are receiving. Doses and schedules vary widely. For methotrexate rescue, timing is critical — the first dose is usually given about 24 hours after your methotrexate infusion begins, and doses continue every 6 hours until your methotrexate blood levels are safe. For colorectal cancer treatment, it is typically given once daily for 5 days during each treatment cycle. Always follow your doctor's exact schedule.
missed_dose: Because this medication is given in a clinical setting, a missed dose is a serious concern — especially when it is being used to 'rescue' you from methotrexate toxicity. If you miss or are late for any scheduled treatment appointment, call your doctor or treatment center IMMEDIATELY. Do not wait. Delaying a rescue dose of levoleucovorin could put your health at serious risk.
storage: You do not need to store this medication at home — it is prepared and stored by healthcare professionals at the clinic or pharmacy. If for any reason you are given vials to bring to an appointment, keep them refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C), protect them from light, and keep them out of reach of children. Do not freeze. Use immediately once mixed/opened, as directed by your pharmacist.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medications you take, including vitamins and supplements. Avoid taking folic acid or folate supplements without your doctor's approval, as this could interfere with your treatment. If you are on methotrexate for a non-cancer condition (like rheumatoid arthritis or psoriasis), do NOT use levoleucovorin unless your doctor specifically instructs you to — it can reduce methotrexate's effectiveness for those conditions. Avoid alcohol, as it can increase the side effects of chemotherapy drugs used alongside levoleucovorin.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: severe allergic reaction (hives, swelling of face or throat, trouble breathing, rapid heartbeat); severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that won't stop; signs of infection such as fever over 100.4°F (38°C), chills, or sore throat; unusual bleeding or bruising; mouth sores that are very painful or prevent you from eating; extreme fatigue or weakness; seizures; confusion or difficulty speaking; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination; or any new or worsening symptoms that worry you. When used for methotrexate rescue, contact your team immediately if you notice any new symptoms between doses.
when_it_works: When used for methotrexate rescue, levoleucovorin starts working right away to protect your healthy cells — you may not feel a noticeable difference, but blood tests your doctor orders will confirm that methotrexate levels are coming down safely. When used with fluorouracil for colorectal cancer, it works together with the chemotherapy over multiple treatment cycles. Your cancer care team will monitor your progress through scans and lab tests over weeks to months to assess how well the treatment is working.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The chemotherapy drugs used with levoleucovorin can harm an unborn baby. Effective birth control is essential during treatment. Kidney problems: If your kidneys do not work well, your doctor will need to monitor you more closely and may adjust your treatment plan. Older adults: Elderly patients may be more sensitive to side effects and may need closer monitoring. Children: Levoleucovorin can be used in children for methotrexate rescue; doses are carefully calculated by the doctor based on the child's body size.
